Lagos Neighbourhoods Basemaps and Drone Imagery
Daily updated vector map that includes 30 data categories: administrative boundaries, road network, building, water features, points of interest, city infrastructure and more.
Basemap is built on OpenStreetMap database, with the following processing and enhancement algorithms applied:
LGA and LCDA administrative boundaries added and clipped to the land boundary (original OSM layer is also preserved),
Included coastlines, drainage, BRT, Waterways and Metro Lines, land and water boundaries,
Added IDs, streets and names of the upper-level features for all administrative boundaries' features (hierarchy of all administrative levels).
Data are 100% ready to go — simply choose a format and get a set up project for your GIS in minutes.

Lagos State Independent Electoral Commission (LASIEC) GIS Unit

The GIS Unit of the Lagos State Independent Electoral Commission (LASIEC) is a strategic division responsible for applying geospatial technologies to electoral management and planning. As the body charged with organizing and supervising local government elections in Lagos State, LASIEC relies on its GIS Unit to ensure accurate mapping of electoral boundaries, polling units, and voter distribution.

The unit plays a vital role in promoting transparency, operational efficiency, and data-driven decision-making in the electoral process. By integrating spatial data into LASIEC’s operations, the GIS Unit helps safeguard the integrity of elections and supports equitable representation across the state’s diverse communities.

The GIS Unit creates and maintains digital maps of electoral wards, local government areas (LGAs), and polling units. These maps are used to guide delimitation, resource allocation, and voter education.
Spatial tools are used to verify the location, accessibility, and coverage of polling units, ensuring that voters are served efficiently and fairly.
GIS data helps analyze population density, voter registration patterns, and demographic trends to support equitable boundary adjustments and logistics planning.
Mapping of transport routes, voting centers, and administrative zones supports the deployment of personnel, materials, and security during elections.
Interactive maps and dashboards allow citizens to locate their polling units, understand ward boundaries, and access election-related information.
The GIS Unit works with other state GIS platforms (e.g., LAGIS) and national bodies like INEC to harmonize spatial data and improve electoral coordination.
The GIS Unit enhances LASIEC’s ability to:
Accurate boundary mapping prevents gerrymandering and supports balanced voter distribution.
Spatial planning reduces logistical errors and improves resource deployment during elections.
Public access to electoral maps builds trust and encourages civic participation.
Geospatial analysis informs policy, boundary reviews, and voter outreach strategies.

Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority (LAMATA) GIS Unit

The GIS Unit of the Lagos Metropolitan Area Transport Authority (LAMATA) is a core technical division responsible for integrating geospatial intelligence into transportation planning, infrastructure development, and mobility management across Lagos State. As the agency tasked with coordinating and implementing the state’s strategic transport vision, LAMATA relies on its GIS Unit to provide accurate spatial data, mapping tools, and location-based analytics that inform decisions and improve service delivery.

The unit operates in synergy with the Lagos State Geographic Information System (LAGIS), ensuring that transport data is harmonized with broader urban planning frameworks. It supports multimodal transport systems including road, rail, water, and non-motorized transport, helping Lagos evolve into a smart and sustainable megacity.

The GIS Unit maps existing and proposed transport corridors, including bus rapid transit (BRT) routes, rail lines, ferry terminals, and pedestrian pathways.
Spatial tools are used to track the condition, usage, and expansion of transport infrastructure such as roads, bridges, terminals, and interchanges.
GIS data supports modeling of traffic patterns, congestion hotspots, and commuter behavior, enabling data-driven interventions.
Geospatial analysis helps assess the feasibility, impact, and alignment of transport projects with land use and population density.
GIS tools assist in route planning, service coverage analysis, and accessibility mapping to improve public transport efficiency.
Supports incident tracking, evacuation planning, and risk assessment for transport-related emergencies.
Interactive maps and dashboards allow the public and stakeholders to explore transport projects, monitor progress, and provide feedback.
The GIS Unit enhances LAMATA’s ability to:
By identifying gaps in transport coverage and optimizing routes, the unit helps reduce travel time and increase access.
GIS data contributes to integrated urban planning, environmental sustainability, and digital governance.
Spatial analytics inform transport policies, investment priorities, and regulatory frameworks.
Transparent mapping and data sharing build trust in government-led transport initiatives.
How to Engage the GIS Unit
Transport planners, researchers, developers, and citizens can engage the GIS Unit by:
Requesting access to transport-related spatial datasets.
Collaborating on mapping projects or mobility studies.
Participating in stakeholder consultations and public forums.
Submitting feedback on transport infrastructure via digital platforms.

Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Authority (LASRERA) GIS Unit

The GIS Unit of the Lagos State Real Estate Regulatory Authority (LASRERA) is a strategic arm dedicated to integrating geospatial technology into real estate regulation and oversight. As part of LASRERA’s mission to promote transparency, accountability, and professionalism in the Lagos property market, the GIS Unit provides spatial data tools that enhance property registration, verification, and monitoring.

By leveraging Geographic Information Systems (GIS), LASRERA ensures that real estate activities are mapped, traceable, and aligned with the state’s urban planning framework. The unit works closely with other GIS-enabled agencies such as LAGIS, LASPPPA, and NTDA to maintain a unified geospatial database for land and property assets.

The GIS Unit maps registered properties across Lagos State, enabling visual verification of location, boundaries, and compliance status. This helps eliminate fraudulent listings and supports due diligence for buyers and investors.
Integration of GIS data into LASRERA’s property database allows users to search, view, and validate real estate assets using interactive maps and satellite imagery.
GIS tools assist in monitoring licensed developers, agents, and property managers by linking their operations to mapped project sites and approved developments.
Spatial analysis of property trends, pricing zones, and development patterns helps LASRERA guide policy decisions and inform stakeholders.
Through GIS-powered dashboards and portals, the public can access verified property data, report suspicious activities, and explore real estate opportunities with confidence.
The GIS Unit strengthens LASRERA’s regulatory capacity by:
Visual verification and spatial tracking of properties help prevent multiple sales, fake titles, and illegal developments.
GIS data supports coordinated development, zoning enforcement, and infrastructure alignment.
Verified geospatial data builds trust among investors, developers, and homebuyers.
Real-time mapping and analytics enable proactive monitoring and enforcement.
How to Engage LASRERA GIS Unit
Stakeholders can engage the GIS Unit by:
Accessing the LASRERA property portal for map-based verification.
Submitting property details for registration and spatial tagging.
Requesting GIS reports for development proposals or investment analysis.
Participating in training and sensitization programs on geospatial tools.

Lagos State Lands Bureau GIS Unit

The GIS Unit of the Lagos State Lands Bureau is a specialized division responsible for integrating geospatial technology into land administration and property management across the state. As Lagos continues to urbanize and expand, the GIS Unit plays a critical role in digitizing land records, mapping property boundaries, and supporting transparent land transactions.

Operating in alignment with the Lagos State Geographic Information System (LAGIS), the unit ensures that land data is accurate, accessible, and interoperable with other government systems. It serves as a backbone for land-related decision-making, policy formulation, and service delivery.

The GIS Unit creates and maintains spatial maps of land parcels, property boundaries, and land use classifications. These maps are essential for planning, dispute resolution, and infrastructure development.
Historical and current land records are digitized and georeferenced, enabling faster access, verification, and updates.
GIS data is used to validate property locations during title registration, ensuring accuracy and preventing overlaps or encroachments.
Spatial data supports land valuation, zoning enforcement, and identification of underutilized or encumbered land.
The unit works closely with LAGIS to ensure that land data is synchronized with other state GIS platforms, enhancing collaboration across ministries.
Through GIS-enabled portals, the public can view land maps, verify property status, and access information on land ownership and availability.
How to Engage the GIS Unit
Citizens, developers, surveyors, and government agencies can engage the GIS Unit by:
Requesting spatial data for land verification or development proposals.
Submitting property details for mapping and georeferencing.
Accessing GIS portals for land status checks and title validation.
Collaborating on land-related research, planning, or digitization projects.
